summary:
# IGNIS – Harmonizing Satellite Fire Observations Across Time

IGNIS is a web-based platform designed to address inconsistencies in long-term satellite fire observation records. Satellite systems such as MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP) have different detection characteristics, making direct comparisons of their hotspot counts potentially misleading. This creates challenges when studying historical fire activity and identifying long-term seasonal or yearly trends.

IGNIS addresses this problem by collecting historical MODIS and VIIRS archives, standardizing their data, and aggregating hotspot detections into monthly counts. Using their overlapping observation period, it calculates seasonal calibration factors to adjust MODIS counts and improve their comparability with VIIRS. These factors are evaluated using a separate held-out validation period.

The resulting harmonized record combines calibrated MODIS estimates for the pre-VIIRS period with actual VIIRS observations for the subsequent period. Through interactive maps, charts, calendars, and anomaly analysis, IGNIS enables users to explore historical hotspot activity across Punjab and Haryana, supporting more consistent long-term analysis and environmental research.
Github: https://github.com/Sh4uryaa/Ignis
details:
What it does and how it works
IGNIS turns 26 years of NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire detections over Punjab and Haryana into one comparable monthly record. The two sensors count fire differently: in Punjab, VIIRS records about 4 to 8 times more detections per month. Joining them directly creates a fake jump in 2012. For each state and calendar month, we calculate the median VIIRS/MODIS ratio on 2012–2022 data. We use it to put the older MODIS record on the VIIRS scale (August 2002 to July 2026). From 2012 on, we use real VIIRS observations. Every estimated month has a 95% bootstrap uncertainty band. A six-page website offers a map, a burning activity calendar, a sensor comparison, anomaly analysis and a methodology page.

Benefits and intended impact
Land managers, scientists, emergency responders and air-quality analysts get a consistent fire history. They can see an area's normal burning seasons, critical periods and unusual months. IGNIS is a planning record, not an alert system.

Tools
Python, Streamlit, Pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, GeoPandas, Shapely, PyDeck, Plotly and Pytest. Data comes from NASA FIRMS (1.75 million detections) and geoBoundaries state borders. There is no database, no external API and no machine learning, on purpose.

Creativity
IGNIS shows its limits as clearly as its results. Estimated, observed, partial and missing months are always labelled, and missing is never shown as zero. We validated on held-out years and report where accuracy drops. On 2023–2026 data, error falls from 75% to 49% in Punjab and from 81% to 34% in Haryana. Accuracy is weaker after 2022, and we show the likely causes, including Terra and Aqua orbit drift, without claiming one.

Factors we considered
Separate factors for each month and state, because the sensor gap changes with the burning season. Confidence filtering with the two scales never treated as equal. Real state boundaries instead of a rectangle. Reproducibility: one command rebuilds every number in about 35 seconds, with 123 automated tests. New regions can be added with one config entry.
